entities.name: PMID:17040962
observations: Early RA cohort: 24/274 had elevated anti-native CII and 9/274 had very high levels; anti-CII-positive patients had higher baseline CRP/ESR, not later. In 8/9 with very high baseline levels, antibody, immune-complex cytokine induction, CRP, and ESR declined in parallel over follow-up.

entities.name: PMID:28336519
observations: In 773 RA patients, anti-CII associated with elevated CRP, ESR, swollen joint count, DAS28 and DAS28-CRP at diagnosis and up to 6 months; over 5 years it associated with improvement and better EULAR response, indicating early but not persistent inflammatory activity.

entities.name: PMID:22548748
observations: In an early RA cohort of 256, anti-CII-positive patients had higher CRP and ESR at diagnosis, but not during follow-up; baseline anti-CII was associated with early radiographic damage.

entities.name: Anti-CII early RA activity
observations: In early RA, anti-CII positivity marks a short-lived inflammatory phenotype: CRP, ESR, swollen joints and DAS28 are higher at diagnosis/early months, while inflammation tends to decline; it is not a reliable marker of sustained activity.
